product_context:
Internal brief only. Do not dump this into the email.

WHAT IT IS: a short description of the product.
WHO TO WRITE: the people who live with the workflow, not commentators or vendors selling the same thing.
TRIGGER TO INFER: live work on the problem, even if they never named your product.
EMAIL SHAPE: one observed fact → why you are writing → one low-friction ask.
Never invent customers, launches, or metrics.
sender_block:
=== SENDER (verified for this campaign) ===
- Name: Alex
- Company: Acme
- Current work: one line on what you actually do
- Desired outcome: the conversation you want
- Recipient value: why this is useful to them, not a pitch deck
- Constraints: Apollo FACTS only; no fabricated customers or metrics
=== end sender ===

discovery.what_it_does: One or two sentences: what the product does in the buyer's workflow.
discovery.target_users_or_buyers: Who actually does the work or buys the tool. Named roles and company types beat a vague industry label.
problems_it_solves: The recurring job they already do the hard way
The workaround that costs time or attention
examples_of_problem_signals: A first-person sentence someone might post or say while doing the work
Another concrete complaint, not a category slogan
obvious_non_targets_or_adjacent_vendors: People selling a product in the same category
Commentators describing the problem without owning the workflow
Buyers so large they are not a realistic first customer
discovery.search_guidance: Do not hunt for people asking for the product by name. Hunt for people mid-workflow whose ingredient, tool, or process is still unset.
